title: Jesus Feeds 5,000
subtitle: The story of a hungry crowd, a little boy’s lunch, and a lot of leftovers

next.title: The Lost Sheep
next.sub: Luke 15: a story Jesus told about a shepherd who never stopped looking.

scenes.title: A Hungry Crowd
beats: Everywhere Jesus went, crowds of people followed Him. One day, more than five thousand people came to hear Him on a grassy hill by the sea.
Jesus taught them about God and made sick people well, all day long. But when evening came, everyone was very, very hungry.
“Where can we buy bread for all these people?” Jesus asked His friend Philip. Philip shook his head. “Even if we worked for months, it wouldn’t be enough!”

scenes.title: A Boy’s Lunch
beats: Then Andrew came up with a little boy. The boy had brought his lunch: five small loaves of bread and two little fish.
“Here is a boy with five loaves and two fish,” Andrew said. “But what good is that for so many people?” The boy held out his basket anyway. He wanted to give it to Jesus.

scenes.title: Jesus Gives Thanks
beats: “Have everyone sit down,” Jesus said. So all the people sat down in groups on the soft green grass.
Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up to heaven and thanked God for the food.
Then Jesus began to break the bread and give it out… and it didn’t run out! There was more, and more, and MORE, enough for every single person.

scenes.title: Twelve Baskets
beats: Everyone ate until they were full. Then Jesus said, “Gather up the pieces that are left over, so nothing is wasted.”
The disciples went around with baskets. They filled one… two… three… all the way to twelve baskets of leftovers!
A little boy’s lunch, in Jesus’ hands, became more than enough for everyone. Jesus can do so much with whatever we give Him.

questions: The boy gave Jesus his whole lunch. How do you think he felt when he saw what Jesus did with it?
What is something you could give or share with someone?
Jesus took a little and made it a lot. What little thing could you give to Jesus?

verse.text: I am the bread of life.
